summary: This note covers the canonization of Popes John XXIII and John Paul II, both of whom reigned as popes and sovereigns of Vatican City. Their canonizations took place on 27 April 2014. Pope Francis officially approved the decision on 5 July 2013, citing a miracle attributed to John Paul II's intercession for his case, while John XXIII was canonized for opening the Second Vatican Council.
one_line: Covers the 27 April 2014 canonization of Popes John XXIII and John Paul II, and the decisions and miracle behind it.
key_facts: Pope John XXIII lived from 25 November 1881 to 3 June 1963.
Pope John Paul II lived from 18 May 1920 to 2 April 2005.
Pope John XXIII reigned as pope from 1958 to 1963.
Pope John Paul II reigned as pope from 1978 to 2005.
Both popes were sovereigns of Vatican City.
The canonizations of Pope John XXIII and Pope John Paul II were held on 27 April 2014.
Pope Francis made the decision to canonize official on 5 July 2013.
The canonization of Pope John Paul II followed the recognition of a miracle attributed to his intercession.
Pope John XXIII was canonized for his merits in opening the Second Vatican Council.
The date of the canonization was assigned on 30 September 2013.
